subject: Post-demo: Hosting tradeoffs (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) + HIPAA/BAA evidence timeline
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@medsagehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Hosting tradeoffs (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) + HIPAA/BAA evidence timeline

Liam — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your procurement and security teams have a clear path forward: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Use case: PHI extraction + triage routing for intake forms (avg request size ~600 tokens, peak 150 req/s).
- Primary concerns: BAA requirements, SOC 2 artifact evidence, audit log retention, and regional data residency.
- Hosting options discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool), Private VPC/on-prem (full control).

Redwood recommendation (initial):
- Short-term (Q3 PoC): Hosted API behind a scoped BAA with token redaction and strict retention (audit logs kept 90 days) — low lift to validate model accuracy and ops integration.
- Production (target Q4): If procurement requires full isolation for PHI, Dedicated capacity with a customer VPC or Private deployment is preferred. Dedicated gives predictable throughput while letting you enforce tighter networking controls.

Action items I propose (owners & timing):
1) Redwood: Share an evidence checklist and a BAA draft for legal review (attached) — ETA: 48 business hours.
2) MedSage: Confirm whether Procurement requires infrastructure-level isolation (isolated VPC / on-prem) or a BAA with Hosted API is sufficient — ETA: 1 week.
3) Ben (SE): Produce an estimated sizing matrix and a latency/cost projection for Dedicated capacity vs Hosted for your traffic profile — ETA: 3 business days.
4) Marissa (Solutions): Prepare a sample runbook and audit log retention options for both Hosted and Dedicated flows — ETA: 5 business days.

Attachments: Redwood_evidence_checklist_v1.xlsx, BAA_draft_medSage_v0.9.pdf

Questions/notes:
- If Procurement requires SOC 2 in-scope artifacts before signing, we can provide our SOC 2 report and scoped evidence; timelines vary (we can fast-track an evidence package).
- For Private on-prem, we'll need to schedule an infra scoping call (network, HSM/KMS, and air-gap needs) — that typically takes 2–3 weeks to scope.

Would love a quick confirmation on the procurement ask (isolated infra vs BAA) so we can prioritize the evidence you need.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0104

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosting tradeoffs (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) + HIPAA/BAA evidence timeline

Thanks Priya — useful recap. A couple of clarifications from Procurement & Security after our internal sync: 

1) Procurement preference: they will accept Hosted API under a signed BAA for the PoC only if we can get the following commitments in writing:
   - Data retention controls (we need token-level retention policy + ability to purge per-record).
   - Audit log retention: 1 year (searchable) for initial contract.
   - SLA for data access requests (we have a 30-day legal window).

2) Security team asks:
   - Provide SOC 2 report and list of scoped controls (we need to map to our control matrix).
   - Clarify key management: is BYOK/KMS supported for Dedicated and for Private? For Hosted, can you demo envelope encryption?
   - For Dedicated: confirm whether the KV cache is flushed on instance termination; we need assurance for PHI non-persistence beyond configured retention.

3) Timeline: procurement is flexible for PoC but wants a clear path to Dedicated or Private for PROD in case audits require infra isolation. They asked whether Redwood can commit to a project plan and high-level cost delta between Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private.

Can Ben and Marissa provide those items? Also, please note — legal would like the BAA draft to be editable (Word preferred) and to see any exceptions Redwood requires.

Liam
Director of IT Security | MedSage Health
liam.carter@medsagehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-2199
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@medsagehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosting tradeoffs (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) + HIPAA/BAA evidence timeline

Liam — thanks for the specifics. Quick responses inline and updated next-step timeline: 

Procurement asks (responses):
- Token-level retention & per-record purge: Supported. For Hosted API we offer configurable retention windows and a programmatic purge endpoint; we will include the purge SLA language in the BAA draft.
- Audit log retention 1 year: Can accommodate as an add-on for Hosted. For Dedicated and Private you control retention via your logging stack; Redwood will surface and ship logs to your configured storage if requested.
- Data access request SLA: We will add a 30-day response commitment clause to the evidence/BAA draft.

Security asks (responses):
- SOC 2 report: attaching the most recent SOC 2 letter and a control mapping appendix (note: attaching as referenced link in related_links).
- Key management: BYOK/KMS supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations (we'll include config steps in a runbook).
- KV cache persistence: By default KV cache is ephemeral and flushed on instance rotate/terminate; we will include a technical note and configuration options in the Dedicated runbook.

Attached: an editable BAA draft (PDF for initial review; Word will follow on request) and an evidence checklist. Ben / Marissa will follow up with sizing, cost deltas, and a proposed project plan for migrating Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private.

Updated timeline (ETA from today):
- Redwood: Deliver Word BAA, SOC2 copy, and evidence mapping — 48 hours.
- Ben: sizing matrix + cost delta Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — 3 business days.
- Marissa: runbook + KV cache and encryption config notes — 5 business days.

If Procurement wants an additional gating call with our security architect, we can set that up next week (30–45 min).

I will also create a shared folder for evidence items and grant MedSage access.

Appreciate the quick turnaround from your side — we’ll prioritize the items requested.

Best,
Priya
